You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object. KNOWN BUG: When a target sits inside another target's shadow root, the hiding logic walks into that root and hides content inside the outer target. Rules: - Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no". - A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no". - Wording does not matter; the behaviour does. - For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure. === REVIEW 1 FINDINGS === - [blocking] Slotted light children of the target's host are hidden even though they render inside the target. Repro: host `` with shadow `

The walk over the light DOM skips the host (it contains the target through the shadow boundary) but still accepts its light children, which the flat tree places inside the dialog. The criteria say the target and its descendants must not be hidden. The same content in a light-DOM dialog is not hidden. - [minor] Unobserved shadow root with a live announcer hides its host. Repro: host in body with shadow `

Reproduced, but the shadow root is outside the stated criteria, and flag-off behaves the same. - [minor] `ariaHideOutside([null])` throws `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getRootNode')` with the flag on (new `getTargetShadowRoots`). With the flag off it does not throw. Current callers guard against null (useModalOverlay, useComboBox, usePopover), so it is not reached from the library. - [minor] Moving the target into an already-hidden sibling leaves the target inheriting aria-hidden. Reproduced, but the same happens in light DOM, so it is pre-existing and not caused by the diff. - [minor] `acceptRoot === NodeFilter.FILTER_ACCEPT && !isShadowRoot(root)` has a dead second clause, since a shadow root already returns FILTER_SKIP. - [minor] Test "should restore shadow root aria-hidden and stop observing" asserts a negative after one `await Promise.resolve()`, so it passes vacuously if the observer is slow. A `setTimeout` tick would be a sturdier check. - [minor] `keepVisible` does not unhide an element already hidden by the observer (also the light-DOM behavior), so it is only effective for elements added later. === IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) === GOAL: Fix round 1 on the uncommitted shadow-DOM change to packages/@react-aria/overlays/src/ariaHideOutside.ts (see `git diff` in /tmp/ff-eval-jprwy3c6/workspace). The reviewer reproduced a blocking bug; fix it plus two small items, with tests. FILES: packages/@react-aria/overlays/src/ariaHideOutside.ts, packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/ariaHideOutside.test.js (shadow describe block at the end). Fixes: 1. [blocking] Slotted light children rendered inside a target get hidden. Repro (flag on): host `` in body with shadow `

` of the host; `ariaHideOutside([dlg])` (and also with `[t]`-only it's fine to hide p, since the slot isn't inside t). Result: `p` gets aria-hidden though it renders inside the dialog. Fix in `acceptNode`, only when `shadowDOM()` is on: if the node is assigned to a slot (`node.assignedSlot`) and that slot is a target or inside one of the visibleNodes (`nodeContains(visible, slot)`, or the slot itself is in visibleNodes), return FILTER_REJECT (leave it and its subtree visible, like a target descendant). Also cover the MutationObserver path: a light child appended to the host after the call and slotted into the dialog must not be hidden (walk(node) goes through acceptNode, so verify with a test). Keep the flag-off path unchanged. Add tests: initial slotted child inside dialog stays visible; slotted child added later stays visible; a light child of the host that is slotted into a slot OUTSIDE the target (e.g. a second named slot that is a sibling of the dialog in the shadow root) does not need special handling — whatever happens, restore must leave no aria-hidden. 2. [minor] `getTargetShadowRoots` throws on a null entry in targets (flag on only; flag off does not throw). Skip null/undefined targets there. 3. [minor] The test "should restore shadow root aria-hidden and stop observing" asserts a negative after a single `await Promise.resolve()`; wait a real macrotask (e.g. `await act(() => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0)))` or similar matching repo style) so it can't pass vacuously. CONSTRAINTS: Touch only those two files. Use `nodeContains`, not `.contains`. No new deps. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: - With `enableShadowDOM()` on, after `ariaHideOutside([target])` where target is inside a shadow root: every sibling element of the target (and of each ancestor up to the shadow root) inside that shadow root is hidden (aria-hidden="true", or inert when shouldUseInert); light-DOM siblings of the host are hidden; the host itself and every ancestor on the path to the target are NOT hidden; the target and its descendants are not hidden. - Nested shadow roots (target in a shadow root whose host is itself in another shadow root): siblings at every level are hidden; both hosts stay visible. - Content added after the call anywhere in the target's shadow root or any enclosing shadow root (outside the targets and outside already-hidden nodes) gets hidden; content added inside a target does not. - Elements added with `data-live-announcer="true"` or `data-react-aria-top-layer="true"` inside an observed shadow root stay visible; existing such elements inside those shadow roots at call time stay visible. - Multiple targets in different shadow roots (e.g. input in shadow root A, popover in shadow root B, both hosts in body): both targets and both hosts stay visible; all other siblings in A, B, and the light DOM are hidden. - The returned function removes every aria-hidden it added (in light DOM and all shadow roots), leaves pre-existing aria-hidden alone, and stops observing: content added to the shadow roots after restore is not hidden. - Nested calls (observerStack): a second ariaHideOutside call disconnects the first's observers including its shadow-root observers, and restoring the second re-observes all of the first's roots (light and shadow). - With the flag off, behavior is unchanged: all existing tests in ariaHideOutside.test.js pass unchanged, and the flag-off code path does no extra walks or observes. - Tests go in packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/ariaHideOutside.test.js; `yarn eslint` on changed files and `yarn check-types` pass.
